disclosures.title: Saudi Aramco H1 2026 interim report
disclosures.body_text: Official first-half and second-quarter 2026 interim financial report and results.

disclosures.title: Saudi Aramco Q1 2026 interim report
disclosures.body_text: Official first-quarter 2026 interim financial report and results.

disclosures.title: Jafurah midstream minimum-volume commitment
disclosures.body_text: Aramco retained exclusive use of the Jafurah Field Gas Plant and Riyas NGL Fractionation Plant for 20 years under a quarterly volume-based tariff backed by minimum volume commitments. The report does not disclose the committed volume, so no numeric minimum-volume fact is published.

source.filing_type: Annual financial statement notes - dimensional detail

disclosures.title: Guaranteed offshore and onshore rig purchases
disclosures.body_text: At year-end 2025, Aramco-related entities had remaining guaranteed commitments for 18 offshore rigs valued at SAR 22.275 billion and 36 onshore rigs valued at SAR 6.789 billion. The onshore orders include a maximum cancellation exposure of SAR 945 million.

source.filing_type: Annual financial statement notes - dimensional detail

disclosures.title: Saudi Aramco Annual Report 2025
disclosures.body_text: Audited 2025 annual report covering consolidated financial statements, operations, strategy, governance and sustainability performance.

source.filing_type: Annual report supplementary metrics and comparative restatement

disclosures.title: Ordinary-course disputed matters and project support obligations
disclosures.body_text: Aramco reports contingent assets and liabilities arising from contractor claims, lawsuits and arbitrations in the ordinary course of business. Management does not anticipate material adjustments from those matters. The note separately describes support and guarantee arrangements involving Sadara and Petro Rabigh, but does not publish one aggregate contingency amount.

disclosures.title: Global customer base limits geographic credit concentration
disclosures.body_text: Aramco states that its trade receivables arise from a global customer base, limiting geographic concentration of credit risk. It controls counterparty exposure through credit limits, financial-standing reviews, letters of credit, bank guarantees and parent-company guarantees. The report does not disclose a major-customer amount or percentage.

source.filing_type: Annual report customer credit concentration disclosure

disclosures.title: FY 2025 earnings release
disclosures.body_text: Audited annual earnings release with income statement, balance sheet, cash flow, segment and per-share results for 2025 and comparative 2024 amounts.

source.filing_type: Annual report supplementary metrics and comparative restatement

disclosures.title: FY 2025 financial results
disclosures.body_text: 2025 revenue was SAR 1,559.342 billion, net income was SAR 350.210 billion, operating cash flow was SAR 510.798 billion and capital expenditure was SAR 190.444 billion.

source.filing_type: Annual report supplementary metrics and comparative restatement

disclosures.title: 2026 capital investment guidance
disclosures.body_text: Aramco stated 2026 capital investment guidance of USD 50 billion to USD 55 billion.

source.filing_type: Annual report supplementary metrics and comparative restatement

disclosures.title: Fourth quarter 2025 base dividend
disclosures.body_text: The Board declared a fourth-quarter 2025 base dividend of SAR 82.08 billion, equivalent to USD 21.89 billion.

source.filing_type: Annual report supplementary metrics and comparative restatement

disclosures.title: 2026 capital spending peak outlook
disclosures.body_text: Management expects capital spending on currently identified liquids, downstream and new-energy opportunities to peak during 2026. Potential additional spending later in the decade is conditioned on finding accretive opportunities; no amount is asserted by this record.

conditions: potential additional spending would be directed at accretive opportunities
metadata.quote: We expect capital spending on current opportunities including liquids, downstream, and new energies to peak in 2026

source.filing_type: Annual report issuer guidance and targets review

disclosures.title: 2030 sales gas production capacity growth target
disclosures.body_text: Aramco aims to increase sales gas production capacity by approximately 80% by 2030 from the 2021 level. The target is subject to domestic demand and includes pre-FID projects not yet announced.

conditions: inclusive of pre-FID projects not yet announced
metadata.quote: Aramco aims to increase its gas production by approximately 80% by 2030 from 2021 production levels

source.filing_type: Annual report issuer guidance and targets review

disclosures.title: 2030 total gas and associated liquids outlook
disclosures.body_text: Alongside its sales-gas expansion, Aramco anticipates total gas and associated liquids production of approximately 6 mmboed by 2030, including an increase of more than 1 mmbpd in high-value associated liquids.

conditions: anticipated result of the sales-gas capacity growth plan
metadata.quote: the Company anticipates total gas and associated liquids of approximately six mmboed by 2030

source.filing_type: Annual report issuer guidance and targets review

disclosures.title: Jafurah 2030 production ramp targets
disclosures.body_text: Aramco expects the Jafurah development to ramp progressively by 2030 to 2 bscfd of sales gas, 420 mmscfd of ethane and 630 mbpd of high-value liquids and condensates.

metadata.quote: 2 bscfd of sales gas, 420 mmscfd of ethane, and 630 mbpd of high-value liquids and condensates by 2030

source.filing_type: Annual report issuer guidance and targets review

disclosures.title: Fadhili 2027 capacity outlook
disclosures.body_text: The Fadhili Gas Plant expansion is expected to add 1.5 bscfd of raw-gas processing capacity, corresponding to approximately 1.15 bscfd of sales-gas production capacity, by 2027.

metadata.quote: additional raw gas processing capacity of 1.5 bscfd (approximately 1.15 bscfd of sales gas production capacity) by 2027

source.filing_type: Annual report issuer guidance and targets review

disclosures.title: Long-term liquids-to-chemicals capacity goal
disclosures.body_text: Aramco states a long-term goal of increasing capacity at petrochemical-producing complexes to as much as 4 million barrels per day through selected, disciplined liquids-to-chemicals investments. The report does not specify a completion year for this goal.

metadata.quote: with a long-term goal to increase its capacity in petrochemical producing complexes to up to four million barrels per day

source.filing_type: Annual report issuer guidance and targets review

disclosures.title: 2026 Upstream operating outlook
disclosures.body_text: For 2026, Aramco says Upstream will continue growing the gas business, including LNG investments, while maintaining maximum sustainable crude capacity through additional crude increments. This is qualitative issuer outlook rather than quantified earnings guidance.

metadata.quote: Aramco’s Upstream segment will continue to drive growth in its gas business, including LNG investments

source.filing_type: Annual report issuer guidance and targets review

disclosures.title: 2026 Downstream strategic outlook
disclosures.body_text: For 2026, Aramco says Downstream plans to expand and integrate across the hydrocarbon value chain, including strategic refining capacity, liquids-to-chemicals, trading, retail and lubricants. This is qualitative issuer outlook rather than quantified earnings guidance.

metadata.quote: the Downstream segment plans to increase refining capacity in strategic locations

source.filing_type: Annual report issuer guidance and targets review

disclosures.title: 2030 iktva local spending target
disclosures.body_text: After reaching 70% locally sourced supply-chain expenditure in 2025, Aramco set a new target of 75% local spending by 2030 under the iktva program.

metadata.quote: has now established an updated target of 75% local spending by 2030

source.filing_type: Annual report issuer guidance and targets review

disclosures.title: 2050 operational net-zero ambition
disclosures.body_text: Aramco's stated ambition is net-zero Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse-gas emissions by 2050 across wholly owned operated assets. It is recorded as an issuer ambition, not as a guaranteed forecast or an economy-wide Scope 3 target.

metadata.quote: Saudi Aramco’s ambition is to achieve net-zero Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas emissions by 2050 across its wholly-owned operated assets

source.filing_type: Annual report issuer guidance and targets review

disclosures.title: Liquidity management and contractual maturities
disclosures.body_text: Aramco manages liquidity through cash and cash equivalents, available credit facilities, cash-flow forecasts and liquid investments. Security and liquidity are prioritized over yield, and borrowings are monitored by contractual maturity.

metadata.quote: Saudi Aramco’s liquidity risk management includes maintaining sufficient cash and cash equivalents and ensuring the availability of incremental funding through credit facilities

source.filing_type: Annual report governance, industry and risk review

disclosures.title: Antitrust, climate and trade litigation exposure
disclosures.body_text: Aramco reports significant litigation exposure primarily in the United States and Saudi Arabia, including OPEC-related antitrust claims, climate and greenwashing claims, and trade measures affecting exports. Existing OPEC-related cases had been dismissed on sovereign defenses, but future outcomes are not assured.

metadata.quote: Aramco is and has been subject to significant litigation, primarily in the United States and the Kingdom.

source.filing_type: Annual report governance, industry and risk review

disclosures.title: Jafurah, Tanajib and Marjan project milestones
disclosures.body_text: Jafurah commenced production, Tanajib commenced operations, and the Marjan increment came onstream during the period covered by the 2025 report.

source.filing_type: Annual report supplementary metrics and comparative restatement

disclosures.title: Share buyback program
disclosures.body_text: Aramco announced a share buyback program of up to SAR 11.3 billion, equivalent to USD 3 billion, over 18 months.

source.filing_type: Annual report supplementary metrics and comparative restatement

disclosures.title: Hydrocarbon market and production risks
disclosures.body_text: Results are exposed to crude oil and gas prices, global demand, regulation and government production decisions, in addition to operational, project and geopolitical risks.

source.filing_type: Annual report supplementary metrics and comparative restatement

disclosures.title: Crude oil supply, demand and price exposure
disclosures.body_text: Crude oil sales are Aramco's largest revenue component, so international supply, demand and sale prices can materially change operating results and cash flow.

metadata.quote: Aramco’s results of operations and cash flow are significantly impacted by international crude oil supply and demand and the price at which it sells crude oil.

source.filing_type: Annual report governance, industry and risk review

disclosures.title: Asian demand and political concentration
disclosures.body_text: A substantial portion of crude, refined and chemical exports goes to Asian customers; adverse regional economic or political developments could reduce demand and increase competition.

metadata.quote: In 2025 and 2024, customers in Asia, including Company’s affiliated refineries located in Asia, purchased 82% and 81%, respectively, of its crude oil exports.

source.filing_type: Annual report governance, industry and risk review

disclosures.title: Climate transition and net-zero execution
disclosures.body_text: Climate policy, regulation, litigation, investor preferences and substitution may reduce hydrocarbon demand or capital access, while the 2050 Scope 1 and 2 net-zero ambition may require substantial capital and may not be fully achieved.

metadata.quote: Aramco may incur substantial costs and capital expenditures to achieve its net-zero ambition. In addition, Aramco may not fully meet its announced net-zero ambition by 2050.

source.filing_type: Annual report governance, industry and risk review

disclosures.title: Global crude, refining and petrochemical competition
disclosures.body_text: Competitive pressure from national and international oil companies and from refining and petrochemical capacity in served markets can reduce prices, market share and downstream profitability.

metadata.quote: Competitive pressure could have a material adverse impact on the price at which it sells crude oil and other products.

source.filing_type: Annual report governance, industry and risk review

disclosures.title: Operational incidents and critical-asset concentration
disclosures.body_text: Spills, leaks, fires, equipment failure, transportation disruption and natural disasters can harm people and the environment, interrupt operations and create liabilities; key Saudi processing and transport assets increase disruption exposure.

metadata.quote: Aramco is subject to operational risks and hazards that may have a significant impact on its operations or result in significant liabilities and costs.

source.filing_type: Annual report governance, industry and risk review

disclosures.title: Capital-project delivery and return risk
disclosures.body_text: Growth depends on timely and cost-effective project delivery. Funding, permits, contractors, regulation, technology and market assumptions can cause delays, cost overruns, impairments or returns below plan.

metadata.quote: Aramco’s ability to achieve its strategic growth objectives depends on the successful delivery of current and future projects

source.filing_type: Annual report governance, industry and risk review

disclosures.title: Insurance coverage limitations
disclosures.body_text: Aramco primarily self-insures through its captive insurer and does not insure every risk or maintain business-interruption cover for disruptions, creating potential exposure to significant uninsured losses.

metadata.quote: Aramco does not insure against all risks and its insurance may not protect it against liability from all potential events

source.filing_type: Annual report governance, industry and risk review

disclosures.title: Terrorism and armed-conflict exposure
disclosures.body_text: Past attacks affected facilities and temporarily reduced production. Additional attacks or armed conflict could disrupt operations, require significant spending and affect the share price.

metadata.quote: Additional terrorist or other attacks or armed conflict could impact Aramco’s operations and have a material adverse effect

source.filing_type: Annual report governance, industry and risk review

disclosures.title: Hydrocarbon reserve-estimation uncertainty
disclosures.body_text: Proved-reserve estimates depend on interpretations, assumptions, judgments, economic conditions and commercial viability; new information, price changes, regulation or errors can reduce estimated quantity or value.

metadata.quote: Estimates of proved hydrocarbon reserves depend on significant interpretations, assumptions, and judgments.

source.filing_type: Annual report governance, industry and risk review

disclosures.title: IT systems and cybersecurity exposure
disclosures.body_text: Critical information and operational technology supports production, records and communications. Aramco is a high-profile cyber target; it reported that attempts had not been material to financial performance or reputation to date, while future attacks could cause physical, environmental, legal and financial harm.

metadata.quote: Aramco’s systems are a high-profile target for sophisticated cyberattacks by nation states, and criminal hackers

source.filing_type: Annual report governance, industry and risk review

disclosures.title: Government licences, permits and concession dependency
disclosures.body_text: Operations depend on maintaining the Concession and licences, permits and approvals under the Hydrocarbons Law, Energy Supply Law and laws of other jurisdictions. Failure, revocation or termination could interrupt operations and cause penalties.

metadata.quote: Aramco is required to obtain, maintain, and renew Governmental licenses, permits, and approvals in order to operate its businesses.

source.filing_type: Annual report governance, industry and risk review

disclosures.title: 2030 gas growth and crude capacity strategy
disclosures.body_text: Aramco targets growth in sales gas production capacity of more than 80% by 2030 compared with 2021 levels, while maintaining maximum sustainable crude capacity at 12 million barrels per day.

source.filing_type: Annual report supplementary metrics and comparative restatement
